what: Project School Enrollment with Grade Progression Ratios
title: Project School Enrollment with Grade Progression Ratios
text: enrollcast projects school enrollment using cohort survival / grade progression ratio method, implemented matrix projection. works level aggregation (school, district, LEA, city-wide) number grades, operates single grade--year enrollment series. Awesome hex logo provided Adam Higerd.

title: Project School Enrollment with Grade Progression Ratios
text: Install development version GitHub:

title: Project School Enrollment with Grade Progression Ratios
text: Inspect underlying projection matrix time:
code: library(enrollcast)  # Historical grade-level enrollment (long format). history <- data.frame(   year = rep(2021:2023, each = 3),   grade = factor(rep(c("K", "1", "2"), 3), levels = c("K", "1", "2")),   enrollment = c(100, 90, 80, 110, 95, 88, 120, 99, 91) )  # 1. Calculate progression ratios. ratios <- progression_ratios(history, method = "mean") ratios #>   grade_from grade_to     ratio #> 1          K        1 0.9250000 #> 2          1        2 0.9678363  # 2. Project forward. The entry grade (K) is supplied exogenously. base <- history[history$year == 2023, c("grade", "enrollment")] projection <- project_enrollment(   base = base,   ratios = ratios,   horizon = 3,   entry = c(125, 130, 128),   start_year = 2023 ) projection #>   year grade enrollment #> 1 2024     K  125.00000 #> 2 2024     1  111.00000 #> 3 2024     2   95.81579 #> 4 2025     K  130.00000 #> 5 2025     1  115.62500 #> 6 2025     2  107.42982 #> 7 2026     K  128.00000 #> 8 2026     1  120.25000 #> 9 2026     2  111.90607 progression_matrix(ratios) #>       K         1 2 #> K 0.000 0.0000000 0 #> 1 0.925 0.0000000 0 #> 2 0.000 0.9678363 0

title: Project School Enrollment with Grade Progression Ratios
text: enrollcast projects one series per call. project many schools LEAs, split map:
code: # fmt: skip school_history <- data.frame(   school = rep(c("North", "South"), each = 9),   year = rep(2021:2023, each = 3, times = 2),   grade = factor(rep(c("K", "1", "2"), times = 6), levels = c("K", "1", "2")),   enrollment = c(100, 90, 80, 110, 95, 88, 120, 99, 91, 120,                   110, 100, 130, 115, 108, 140, 119, 111) )  projections <- lapply(   split(school_history, school_history$school),   function(df) {     ratios <- progression_ratios(df)     base <- df[df$year == max(df$year), c("year", "grade", "enrollment")]     project_enrollment(base, ratios, horizon = 3, entry = rep(100, 3))   } )  projections$North #>   year grade enrollment #> 1 2024     K  100.00000 #> 2 2024     1  111.00000 #> 3 2024     2   95.81579 #> 4 2025     K  100.00000 #> 5 2025     1   92.50000 #> 6 2025     2  107.42982 #> 7 2026     K  100.00000 #> 8 2026     1   92.50000 #> 9 2026     2   89.52485

Defaults "year", "grade", "enrollment". method summarise per-year ratios one ratio per grade: "mean" (default), "geometric", "median", "last" (recent transition ), "weighted". n_years Optional. Use recent n_years available adjacent-year transitions. n_years exceeds number available transitions, used. weights method = "weighted", finite, non-missing, non-negative numeric vector aligned -recent oldest, one weight per transition year used positive sum. supply weights methods. grade_order Optional character vector giving low--high grade order. omitted, factor levels, numeric ordering, (warning) alphabetical ordering used.

title: Compute grade progression ratios — progression_ratios
code: history <- data.frame(   year = rep(2021:2023, each = 3),   grade = factor(rep(c("K", "1", "2"), 3), levels = c("K", "1", "2")),   enrollment = c(100, 90, 80, 110, 95, 88, 120, 99, 91) ) progression_ratios(history) #>   grade_from grade_to     ratio #> 1          K        1 0.9250000 #> 2          1        2 0.9678363  # For method = "weighted", weights align most-recent to oldest: here the # 2022->2023 transition gets weight 2 and 2021->2022 gets weight 1. progression_ratios(history, method = "weighted", weights = c(2, 1)) #>   grade_from grade_to     ratio #> 1          K        1 0.9166667 #> 2          1        2 0.9645224  # The same K -> 1 ratio via stats::weighted.mean(). Unlike `weights` # above, weighted.mean() pairs each weight with the value at the same # position, and the per-year ratios run oldest to newest -- so the # weights must be reversed to line up. k_ratios <- c(95 / 100, 99 / 110) # 2021->2022, then 2022->2023 stats::weighted.mean(k_ratios, rev(c(2, 1))) #> [1] 0.9166667

title: Project enrollment forward — project_enrollment
text: Projects grade-level enrollment forward arbitrary horizon using grade progression ratio method. Internally builds projection matrix ratios advances enrollment one year time (one matrix-vector product per projected year), overwriting entry grade supplied exogenous value year. ratios optional schedule supplied.

Matrix row column names must unique identical order; steps must use names. step's entry must NULL one finite, non-negative number. start_year Optional integer label base year; output years run start_year + 1. explicit value resulting years must within R integer range. enrollcast 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-08-26 Initial CRAN release. progression_ratios() computes progression ratios historical grade-level enrollment, mean, geometric, median, last, weighted summaries. warns calendar-year gaps across complete supplied history n_years selects recent transitions. progression_matrix() places ratios sub-diagonal square projection matrix, leaving entry-grade row zero. project_enrollment() advances base enrollment vector arbitrary horizon, either ratios prebuilt schedule, overwriting exogenous entry grade year. Missing schedule coefficients preserved aggregate warning rather imputed. swing_schedule() builds per-year schedules hold enrollment flat swing years, apply recovery multipliers, resume normal projection.
